releaseNotes: Platform release: a company's economics stop being sentences. Price, what a customer costs to serve, what one costs to win, churn, cash on hand and monthly spend are structured inputs, and gross margin, monthly contribution, how long a customer stays, what one is worth, worth against cost to win, payback, runway, and customers to break even all follow from them. A founder can model more than one scenario and compare them.

Two rules carry the design. A derived figure is never stored — every one is recomputed from the inputs on read, because a stored derivation is a second copy of the truth that drifts the moment somebody edits a price and nobody recomputes, which is the exact contradiction this product exists to prevent. And a figure with a missing input is absent rather than zero, and says which input it is waiting for: a margin of 0% and "you have not said what a customer costs you" lead to entirely different conversations, and in a company still working this out the second is far more common. Zero churn is reported as unbounded rather than infinite, a cost above the price is a real negative margin rather than an error, and money is held in minor units as integers so a planning model cannot accumulate float error and disagree with itself about a number the founder typed exactly. A sensitivity pass names which assumption the plan actually rests on, loudest first, and stays silent about inputs the figure does not depend on at all. Checks, 227 domain tests, the production build, and the full audit pass.
